Q1: Nitromethane exhibits known hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive toxicity, oral toxicity, and organ/systemic toxicity. It also presents expanded hazards (Tier 2) for environmental, inhalation, and dermal/eye concerns. Data on endocrine disruption hazards are currently deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: Nitromethane is listed on California's Proposition 65 as a chemical known to cause cancer or reproductive harm, and is classified by IARC as a Group 2B possible human carcinogen. These listings highlight significant health concerns for this chemical.
Q3: Nitromethane is extensively characterized, with 22,000 literature references and a well-defined molecular structure. Although it lacks an IRIS evaluation, it has a Provisional Peer-Reviewed Toxicity Value (PPRTV) and 53 toxicity records, indicating significant toxicological study.
